question: Should opaque `channelData` be removed in full whenever any nested key or value contains protected runtime context?
rationale: Generic core code cannot safely understand every provider's native payload schema, so choosing between whole-payload suppression, action rejection, or selective sanitation defines a security and message-delivery contract that requires owner intent.

options.title: Approve whole-payload suppression
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior, explicitly accepting that mixed safe and protected native metadata is discarded to avoid leaking internal context.

options.title: Reject the send action
options.body: Return a clear suppression result instead of silently sending the remaining visible content without its native metadata.

options.title: Design typed channel sanitation
options.body: Pause this PR until channel-owned schemas can identify safely removable text fields without interpreting arbitrary opaque payloads in core.

recommendation.title: Approve whole-payload suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior, explicitly accepting that mixed safe and protected native metadata is discarded to avoid leaking internal context.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail covers the outbound lifecycle, message-tool source replies, structured payload handling, and repository ownership.
